case_prompt:
<case_prompt>
A young male with a history of untreated human immunodeficiency virus infection presents for clinical evaluation with a sudden onset of progressive blurring of vision in both eyes. Over the preceding year, he had been self-administering intravenous dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, and vitamin C, as well as high-dose oral multivitamins and minerals. On examination, best-corrected visual acuity is 6/60 in the right eye and 6/48 in the left eye. Anterior segment examination is normal bilaterally. Ophthalmoscopy demonstrates +2 vitreous cells, large areas of dense white retinal opacification, retinal exudates, vasculitis, and scattered preretinal hemorrhages in both eyes. General physical examination reveals blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg, right-sided hemiparesis requiring assistance for ambulation, an intergluteal ulcer, and a widespread, generalized pruritic cutaneous eruption.
</case_prompt>

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Cutaneous eruption in a patient injecting illicit intramuscular/intravenous steroids and high-dose vitamins could represent a hypersensitivity drug reaction or severe seborrheic dermatitis; ruled out by physical diagnostic confirmation of widespread ectoparasitic infestation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: There were generalized scabies and an intergluteal ulcer present.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Clinical examination identifying generalized scabies along with bilateral necrotizing retinitis, prompting directed topical treatment with permethrin cream alongside systemic and intravitreal ganciclovir therapy.
